summary: The Spark delta lane is healthy (lastDeltaSuccessAt 2026-09-22T19:33Z, 2.9 min old; price_history/listing_history/activity_events all written at 19:48Z) and the cache tables are fresh and stamped v3-2026-05-07 (market_pulse_live 45 rows updated 19:33-19:34Z; market_stats_cache computed 19:45Z). The foundation's real problem is load, not freshness. pg_cron runs three overlapping refresh jobs: refresh_listing_tile_mv_30min at :02/:32 takes 387-471 s per run, refresh_dal_mvs_15min at :05/:20/:35/:50 takes 234-347 s, post_sync_pipeline every 15 min 19-223 s; that is about 2,100 s of refresh work per hour (58% of wall clock). Postgres logged 954 'canceling statement due to statement timeout' in 24 h, all from PostgREST, and 51% of them fall in minutes :00-:14 of each hour, exactly the window where those jobs plus the hourly Vercel /api/cron/refresh-mvs duplicate all run. The queries that die are user-facing: listing_tile_mv tile reads (327), the /housing-market/bend financing-mix RPC (179), five amenity-page DALs that bounding-box scan raw listings (133), listing_history reads (98), getAtlasTiles keyset over raw listings (83), and the sitemap's zip enumeration over raw listings (42, which silently drops every /zip/ URL from the sitemap on failure). Vercel recorded 7,602 + 2,534 Server-Components render errors (549 users) on /cities/bend/boyd-acres, /cities/bend/summit-west, /communities/juniper-preserve and /cities/bend in 48 h, plus 2,555 'Failed to load static file for page: /500' because the fallback error page does not exist; the same pages answer 200 in 0.4-0.6 s outside the refresh windows, so crawlers get intermittent 500s. RUM (web_vitals, 60,000 rows 2026-09-17..22) shows LCP p75 above 2.5 s on every public class: neighborhood 12.5 s, zip 11.6 s, search 8.2 s, community 6.1 s, home 4.6 s, subdivision 4.5 s, city 3.1 s; TTFB p75 subdivision 2.6 s; place-page HTML is 1.9-3.8 MB. Accuracy: refresh_community_market_pulse still writes impossible neighborhood months-of-supply (Summit West 48.6 on 81 actives, Century West 50.0, Pronghorn 66.0) that pages withhold only through a grain gate; six copy-pasted medianListPrice() functions compute 'median list price' on amenity pages from raw scans outside the engine; a second mt-v1 shadow engine runs on three crons. Cron fleet: 76 registered, 15 orphan routes (including sync-verify-full-history, whose absence stalled strict verification 160 days with a 305-row backlog), three dead performance-pull crons reading producer rows last executed 2026-08-18, loop-sentinel firing 144 no-op runs/day into sync_logs, and refresh-mvs returning 24 5xx in 48 h. Schema: 160 tables with RLS and no policy, 12 SECURITY DEFINER views flagged, 256 unused indexes (11 on listings), 10 duplicate indexes, dead tables from FUB/producer/video eras, and the auto-generated schema/coverage docs 13 and 31 days stale. Advisor and Vercel figures were captured once before the orchestrator banned MCP tools and could not be re-observed.

findings.title: Materialized-view refresh duty cycle starves the database; place and search pages throw 500s in the refresh windows
findings.claim: pg_cron runs ~2,100 s of REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW work per hour (tile MV 387-471 s twice an hour, dal MVs 234-347 s four times an hour, pipeline 19-223 s four times), and during those windows PostgREST reads on listing_tile_mv, listings, listing_history and RPCs hit the statement timeout (954 in 24 h, 51% inside minutes :00-:14). The effect on users and crawlers is 7,602 + 2,534 Server-Components render errors and 2,555 missing-/500-page errors on /cities/bend, /cities/bend/boyd-acres, /cities/bend/summit-west and /communities/juniper-preserve in 48 h, while the same URLs answer 200 in 0.4-0.6 s between refreshes.
findings.evidence: cron.job + cron.job_run_details rows (jobs 164/163/146 durations, 14:42-19:39Z); query_logs: 954 timeouts, 5-minute buckets :00 170 / :05 213 / :10 104 vs :15 14; Vercel get_runtime_errors 48h clusters (7,602/549 users; 2,555/570 users); live curl 200s at 19:49-19:55Z; docs/plans/F7-sync-contention.md header (fix applied 2026-07-29, 'honest residual' ~390 s read cost remains); supabase/migrations/20260729193000_listing_tile_mv_drop_now_refreshed_at.sql; mv_refresh_state listing_tile_mv_src 19:39:29Z.
findings.why_it_matters: Googlebot and AI crawlers that hit a place page in a refresh window receive a 500 (and a broken error page); repeated 5xx demotes and eventually drops URLs, and it matches the subdivision-heavy 5xx list in Vercel. It also inflates LCP/TTFB on every class. This is the single largest mechanical suppressor of visibility found in the data layer.
findings.proposed_fix: Split listing_tile_mv into an on-market MV (~10K rows, refresh every 15 min in seconds) and a terminal MV (594K rows, refresh nightly during the 08:00-12:00Z low-traffic trough visible in the hourly timeout series); reschedule job 163 so it never overlaps 164; delete the hourly Vercel /api/cron/refresh-mvs duplicate (DATA-2); move the request-time raw-listings scans in DATA-3 onto the MVs; and only then decide on a compute upgrade or read replica (Matt). Add a real fallback error page so a render error returns a branded 500 with retry, not ENOENT.

findings.title: Hourly Vercel /api/cron/refresh-mvs duplicates the pg_cron MV refresh, overlaps it, and fails with 5xx
findings.claim: vercel.json schedules /api/cron/refresh-mvs at :08 every hour; it calls refresh_listing_tile_mv, refresh_geo_snapshot_mv, refresh_listing_boundary_xref_mv, refresh_listing_search_mv and refresh_neighborhood_year_pricing_mv through PostgREST while pg_cron jobs 164 (:02, ~7 min) and 163 (:05, ~4.5 min) are refreshing the same views. refresh_listing_tile_mv() skips with ok:true when job 164 still holds advisory lock 7101, but when 164 has finished by :08 the Vercel call acquires the lock and runs a third full ~7-minute tile refresh through PostgREST (observed once as a PostgREST statement timeout of refresh_listing_tile_mv()); the other four RPCs run regardless. The route returned HTTP 5xx 24 times in 48 h and its header comment still says 'every 15 minutes' and '~30-40 s'.
findings.evidence: app/api/cron/refresh-mvs/route.ts:7-11,26-30,60-64,136-150; vercel.json '8 * * * *'; cron.job rows 163/164 with schedules and 387-471 s / 234-347 s durations; supabase/migrations/20260729193000_listing_tile_mv_drop_now_refreshed_at.sql:326-345 (pg_try_advisory_lock(7101) → returns {ok:true, skipped:true} on a miss); Vercel get_runtime_logs group_by requestPath statusCode 5xx 48h → /api/cron/refresh-mvs 24; query_logs one PostgREST 'refresh_listing_tile_mv()' statement timeout. Whether the geo/xref/search refresh functions hold their own advisory locks, and the exact 500 reason, are UNVERIFIED (the Vercel log query timed out twice before the MCP ban).
findings.why_it_matters: A third concurrent refresh of an 812 MB MV in the worst minute of the hour extends the starvation window in DATA-1 and burns a 5-minute Vercel function every hour for nothing; only neighborhood_year_pricing_mv is not already covered by pg_cron.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove refresh-mvs from vercel.json and move refresh_neighborhood_year_pricing_mv() into pg_cron job 163 after refresh_listing_search_mv (it derives from listing_tile_mv); delete or archive the route; update the check-cron-registered baseline.

findings.title: Public pages still scan the 597K-row listings table at request time (amenity pages, atlas, listing bundles, financing mix)
findings.claim: Six amenity detail DALs (parks/trails/golf/events/venues/schools) bounding-box scan raw listings and compute their own median; getAtlasTiles keysets raw listings for closed sales per city; getListingDetailBundles reads listing_history by event_date; /housing-market/bend calls analytics_financing_mix_co with an 8 s cap. These shapes account for 133 + 83 + 98 + 179 = 493 of the 954 statement timeouts in 24 h and surface as '[build-place-atlas] read failed' (394 errors, 123 users), getParkDetail timeouts, getFinancingMix failures and 'short read is not cached' revalidation loops.
findings.evidence: query_logs shape counts; lib/data/parks/getParkDetail.ts:132-147 and the five twins; lib/data/listings/getAtlasTiles.ts:186-204; lib/data/listings/getListingDetailBundles.ts:107-322; lib/data/analytics/getFinancingMix.ts:60 + supabase/migrations/20260827120000_analytics_financing_mix_rpc.sql (SET statement_timeout '8s'); Vercel error clusters [build-place-atlas] 394, getParkDetail 6/4/3/2, getFinancingMix 13; CLAUDE.md §7 rule 6 'Don't aggregate raw listings … use the cache'.
findings.why_it_matters: These are the reads that die first when the refresh runs, and they sit on indexable pages (parks, trails, golf, /housing-market/bend, /search). Each failure either throws (500) or caches a thin page for the TTL. They also violate the one-engine rule for medians (§0).
findings.proposed_fix: Read the amenity home tiles from listing_tile_mv (it carries lat/lng and status) or from a small precomputed amenity_homes MV; take the median from the engine (getMarketPulse / market_stats_cache) instead of six local functions; precompute the closed-sales atlas per city into an MV refreshed nightly; give getFinancingMix a cached table written by the daily stats cron rather than a request-time RPC; keep the existing makeResilientCached wrappers.

findings.title: The sitemap enumerates ZIPs and cities by scanning raw listings and silently drops those URLs when the scan times out
findings.claim: app/sitemap.ts builds the /zip/ leg with fetchAllRows over listings (SELECT PostalCode … WHERE StandardStatus IS NULL OR ilike … LIMIT/OFFSET) and a similar City enumeration; those shapes timed out 42 and 11 times in 24 h, and the leg() wrapper returns [] on failure, so an entire URL family vanishes from the sitemap for that hour's cache without any error surfaced.
findings.evidence: app/sitemap.ts:470-539 (leg('zips', fetchAllRows(supabase,'listings','PostalCode', q.or(ACTIVE_STATUS_OR).not('PostalCode','is',null)), [])); query_logs shapes 'SELECT PostalCode FROM listings' 42 and 'SELECT City FROM listings' 11 statement timeouts; comment at :470 'a transient DB error thins the sitemap instead of fabricating entries'.
findings.why_it_matters: A sitemap that intermittently omits whole families teaches Google that those URLs are unstable; the zip pages already show 11.6 s LCP p75, so they are doubly disadvantaged. The listings leg was fixed 2026-09-16 with a partial index (migration 20260916080000) but the zip/city legs were not.
findings.proposed_fix: Enumerate ZIPs and cities from listing_tile_mv (indexed, on-market only) or from geo_snapshot_mv / boundaries geo_type='zip' (migration 20260910013000 added zip boundaries), never from raw listings; log a site_signal row when any leg returns [] so a thinned sitemap becomes a measurable event.

findings.title: Field LCP p75 is above 2.5 s on every public route class; neighborhood 12.5 s, search 8.2 s, community 6.1 s; place HTML is 2-4 MB
findings.claim: web_vitals (60,000 rows, 2026-09-17..22) puts LCP p75 at neighborhood 12,484 ms, zip 11,588, search 8,244, community 6,052, home 4,572, subdivision 4,548, place-type 4,136, market-blog 3,504, city 3,136, listing 2,548; TTFB p75 subdivision 2,628 ms and search 2,080 ms; /cities/bend serves 3.77 MB of HTML, /cities/bend/summit-west 2.14 MB.
findings.evidence: scratch db-reads.mjs table (notes §4); curl size_download for /cities/bend 3,773,923 B, /cities/bend/summit-west 2,144,553 B, /cities/bend/boyd-acres 1,915,329 B; worst paths /communities/caldera-springs 19.5 s (n 22), /homes-for-sale 16.7 s (n 104), /about 15.7 s (n 72).
findings.why_it_matters: Core Web Vitals is a ranking signal and a crawl-budget input; every class fails 'good'. TTFB above 2 s on subdivision and search says the server render itself (DAL reads under DATA-1/DATA-3) is the floor, before any front-end work.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat TTFB as the data-layer KPI: after DATA-1..3, cap place-page HTML (defer the full plat/home lists behind pagination or client fetch, drop inlined JSON-LD duplicates), and make the loop's measurer ingest the per-class p75 from web_vitals weekly so regressions become nodes.

findings.title: The fallback error page does not exist in the production build, so a render error becomes a raw ENOENT 500
findings.claim: When a Server Component throws (DATA-1), Next tries to serve /var/task/.next/server/pages/500.html and fails: 2,555 'Failed to load static file for page: /500 ENOENT' errors reaching 570 users in 48 h. app/error.tsx and app/global-error.tsx exist but do not cover this path.
findings.evidence: Vercel runtime error cluster (count 2,555, users 570, routes /cities/bend/boyd-acres, /cities/bend/summit-west, /communities/juniper-preserve, /cities/bend); ls app/error.tsx app/global-error.tsx app/not-found.tsx present, no pages/ dir.
findings.why_it_matters: A crawler or visitor gets an unstyled failure with no retry, no navigation and no brand; the second-largest error cluster on the site is the error page itself.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a pages/500.tsx (or the Next-version-appropriate static 500) so the fallback exists, and verify the app-router error boundary catches errors thrown in layout/metadata paths (wrap the DAL reads that can throw in generateMetadata with the existing withTimeoutFallback).

findings.title: refresh_community_market_pulse writes impossible neighborhood months-of-supply into a served cache table every 15 minutes
findings.claim: market_pulse_live neighborhood rows carry months_of_supply 48.60 (Summit West, 81 actives), 50.00 (Century West), 32.40 (Awbrey Butte), 66.00 (Pronghorn) with a v3 methodology stamp, because the writer's numerator is polygon-based and its denominator is a SubdivisionName text join; the city row Terrebonne reads 30.00 on 5 actives with no minimum-sample guard. Pages withhold these only through a per-call-site publish gate.
findings.evidence: market_pulse_live row read 19:34Z; lib/market/geo-grain-trust.ts:1-40 (measured 2026-08-19 counts: century-west 2 via alias vs 42 in polygon); lib/market/publish-months-of-supply.ts:14-25 ('withhold'); app/cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug]/page.tsx:493 monthsOfSupply: null; lib/market/classify.ts:23 only guards closedLast6Months <= 0; lib/data/market/getMarketPulseJsonFeed.ts exposes months_of_supply.
findings.why_it_matters: §0 says a number that cannot be verified does not ship; here the wrong number is computed, stamped and stored on a schedule, and correctness depends on every consumer (JSON feed, CRM market report, CMA, narratives) remembering the gate. One missed call site publishes a buyer's-market verdict on a district that turns over in ten weeks.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the writer honest: in refresh_community_market_pulse set months_of_supply, absorption_rate_pct and the sold-derived columns to NULL for untrusted grains (or compute closes from the same polygon via a terminal-status xref), add a minimum-closes guard (registry minN 30 already exists in lib/data/market-truth/registry.ts:47) at the writer and in classify.ts, and add a check to market-stat-consistency that fails when any pulse row implies more 6-month closes than the 12-month sold count.

findings.title: More than one statistics engine still produces public numbers (six local medians, mt-v1 shadow crons, SQL pulse, SQL period stats)
findings.claim: Despite the 2026-08-17 mission ('only one source of statistics … always through this engine'), public medians on six amenity page types are computed locally over raw scans, months-of-supply is computed in classify.ts, refresh_market_pulse(), refresh_community_market_pulse() and compute_and_cache_period_stats, and a separate mt-v1 shadow engine runs on three 6-hourly crons (compute-neighborhood-metrics, compute-subdivision-metrics, refresh-sale-pricing-facts → compute_market_metrics_shadow, which timed out 8 times in 48 h).
findings.evidence: grep results in notes §2: lib/data/{parks,trails,golf,events,venues,schools}/get*Detail.ts medianListPrice(); lib/data/analytics/rebuildAnalyticsMarts.ts:78; lib/data/listings/getRepeatSalesAppreciation.ts:48; lib/data/proof/outcomes.ts:126; vercel.json compute-* crons; docs/plans/STATISTICS_ENGINE_MISSION.md; Vercel cluster '[refresh-sale-pricing-facts] compute_market_metrics_shadow upstream request timeout' 8.
findings.why_it_matters: Two engines means two answers for the same place on two pages, which is the exact §0 failure class, and the shadow engine's crons add load to the same starved database without any page reading them yet.
findings.proposed_fix: Either promote mt-v1 to the one engine and retire refresh_market_pulse/compute_and_cache_period_stats, or freeze mt-v1 and stop its crons until a page consumes it; route every JS median through lib/data/proof/outcomes.ts medianCont or the SQL percentile_cont in one RPC; add a gate that fails any new `function median` in lib/data outside the engine module.

findings.title: Strict history verification stalled for 160 days because its cron route was never registered; 15 cron routes are orphans
findings.claim: sync-verify-full-history last ran 2026-04-15 with a 305-row backlog (303 expired); the route exists but is not in vercel.json, along with sync-parity, start-sync, refresh-listing-year-stats, detect-expired-listings, studio-slate, neighborhood-default-subscriptions and the eight marketing-snapshot-* fan-out targets. sync-status-report.mjs still reads two dropped MVs (PGRST205) and docs/SYNC.md describes cadences (2-min Inngest delta, 10-min full sync) that do not match vercel.json (15-min delta, weekly full).
findings.evidence: sync-status-report runTelemetry stalled 230,365 min; python diff app/api/cron vs vercel.json (15 orphans); warnings listing_year_finalization_stats PGRST205; docs/SYNC.md:7-8,50 vs vercel.json sync-delta '3,18,33,48' and sync-full '0 2 * * 0'; SYNC_HANDOFF_PLAYBOOK.md:42-70 names unregistered lanes.
findings.why_it_matters: Not a visibility blocker (expired listings' history is not on indexable pages), but it is the class the process canon calls 'dead code wearing a schedule's clothes', and an agent told to 'fix sync' will follow SYNC.md into commands that do not run.
findings.proposed_fix: Register sync-verify-full-history at a low cadence until the 305 rows drain, then remove it; delete the other orphan routes or register them; fix sync-status-report to stop reading dropped MVs; rewrite SYNC.md cadences from vercel.json; shrink the check-cron-registered baseline accordingly.

findings.title: Dead and no-op crons: three performance-pull jobs, loop-sentinel with the kill switch off, producer-era optimization report
findings.claim: performance-pull-48h/7d/30d run daily to read marketing_brain_actions status='executed' whose last row is 2026-08-18 (producers deleted 2026-09-07) and write content_performance, which holds 6 all-null rows from 2026-06-16; loop-sentinel fires 144 times a day with LOOP_SENTINEL=off and fills 93% of sync_logs with skip rows; marketing-optimization-report (weekly) is a producer-era email built on getDashboardMarketingData.
findings.evidence: helper reads of marketing_brain_actions (status executed, latest 2026-08-18T14:01Z) and content_performance (6 rows, measured_at 2026-06-16, impressions null); sync_logs 24h aggregate 144/155 'loop_sentinel:skip 204 kill switch (LOOP_SENTINEL=off)'; app/api/cron/performance-pull-48h/route.ts header; app/api/cron/marketing-optimization-report/route.ts imports; CLAUDE.md §5.
findings.why_it_matters: Each is a Vercel invocation and a DB round trip that produces nothing, and the sentinel noise makes sync_logs useless as the cron ledger the SYNC docs say it is; a 'run the loop' session reading sync_logs sees 144 kill-switch rows and no real signal.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the three performance-pull crons and marketing-optimization-report from vercel.json (archive routes); make loop-sentinel exit without logging when the kill switch is off, or unregister it while off; document that cron health is read from Vercel runtime errors + postgres logs, not sync_logs.

findings.title: Schema hygiene: 160 RLS-without-policy tables, 12 SECURITY DEFINER views, 256 unused and 10 duplicate indexes, dead FUB/producer/video tables
findings.claim: Advisors flag rls_enabled_no_policy on 160 tables, security_definer_view ERROR on 12 views that public pages read (listing_tile_mv, geo_snapshot_mv, listing_boundary_xref_mv, similar_listings_mv, site_signal, target_query_benchmark…), 256 unused indexes including 11 on listings that every delta upsert maintains, and 10 duplicate indexes (market_pulse_live, market_stats_cache, boundaries, listing_history…). Dead or orphan tables remain: listings_historical 0, listing_photo_classifications 0, listing_sync_status 0, listing_views 0, open_houses 20 rows last written 2026-04-03, fub_person_geo 2,255 rows after the FUB decommission, producer_change_requests/producer_execution_failures, content_briefs 987, hero_videos, video_tours_cache.
findings.evidence: get_advisors performance/security parsed counts (single capture, UNVERIFIED after MCP ban); helper counts in notes §6; docs/DATA_COVERAGE_INDEX.md:48-58,102-109.
findings.why_it_matters: Unused indexes on listings add write cost to every 15-minute delta and to the MV refresh diff; duplicate indexes on the cache tables do the same on every pipeline run; dead tables and security-definer views are the surface an agent or a policy audit trips over. None of it blocks visibility directly.
findings.proposed_fix: One migration: drop the 10 duplicate indexes and, after confirming pg_stat_user_indexes idx_scan=0 over a full week, the unused listings indexes; drop or archive the dead tables (open_houses, listings_historical, listing_photo_classifications, listing_sync_status, listing_views, producer_*, fub_person_geo after export); review the 12 security-definer views with security_invoker where anon reads are intended (migration 20260921120000 already did this for sale_pricing_facts_sfr).

findings.title: The auto-generated data docs an agent must read before writing SQL are 13-31 days stale and wrong on live facts
findings.claim: DATABASE_SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT is dated 2026-09-09 with six later migrations; DATA_COVERAGE_INDEX is dated 2026-08-22 and calls listing_videos DEAD (31 rows, written 2026-09-21); DATABASE_FOR_AI_AGENTS says market_stats_cache refreshes every 6 h (every 15 min by pg_cron plus daily) and that market_pulse_live has no neighborhood rows (28 exist); SPARK_FIELDS_AUDIT points at a deleted sync file. G16 (ci:data-access) only runs locally/nightly with creds and has not run.
findings.evidence: docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT.md:3; ls supabase/migrations tail; docs/DATA_COVERAGE_INDEX.md:48,116; docs/DATABASE_FOR_AI_AGENTS.md:125,204,704; docs/SPARK_FIELDS_AUDIT.md:11; post_sync_pipeline_runs result.stats runs 60 at 19:45Z; helper count listing_videos 31.
findings.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md §7 forbids schema discovery and makes these docs the only permitted source; when they are wrong, every session (Grok, Cursor, Claude) reasons from the same stale picture, which is exactly how 'the plats are not ingested' happened.
findings.proposed_fix: Run the G16 refresh on a registered nightly cron (or a GitHub Action with the read-only creds) so the snapshot, DAL index and coverage index regenerate and commit automatically; fix the three prose claims in DATABASE_FOR_AI_AGENTS.md; retire SPARK_FIELDS_AUDIT.md or regenerate it from lib/sync/deltaSync.ts EXPAND.

findings.title: Unique Spark information is ingested but not stored where pages can use it (open houses, videos, prior listings)
findings.claim: deltaSync expands Photos, FloorPlans, Videos, VirtualTours, OpenHouses, Documents and CustomFields into listings.details, but the queryable side is thin: open_houses table 20 rows (last 2026-04-03) while the live read scans the listings.OpenHouses column (15 timeouts/24 h); listing_videos holds 31 rows for ~7.5K actives; listings_historical is empty so 'previously listed at' and re-list history never reach a page; the SPARK_FIELDS_AUDIT gap list (HOA, schools, garage, taxes, zoning) was never closed in the doc.
findings.evidence: lib/sync/deltaSync.ts:71; lib/spark.ts:697-735; helper counts listing_videos 31 / open_houses 20 / listings_historical 0; query_logs shape 'SELECT ListingKey, City, OpenHouses FROM listings' 15 timeouts; docs/SPARK_FIELDS_AUDIT.md:63-98; app/listing/[listingKey]/page.tsx:375 getListingVideos with 8 s fallback.
findings.why_it_matters: Open houses, video tours and prior-listing history are the on-page facts competitors and answer engines reward, and they are the depth Matt says the database has; today they live in TOASTed JSON that cannot be scanned and are read through the slowest path.
findings.proposed_fix: Have deltaSync write open houses and videos to their tables on every upsert (the syncWrites helpers exist) and read /open-houses and listing pages from those tables; ingest Spark /historical for on-market listings into listings_historical; regenerate the fields audit from the actual EXPAND list.

findings.title: PDF report routes fail in production: @react-pdf/stylesheet is missing from the bundle
findings.claim: /api/pdf/report and /api/reports/export threw 'Cannot find package @react-pdf/stylesheet imported from /var/task/node_modules/@react-pdf/layout/lib/index.js' 42 times for 21 users in 48 h (6 5xx on /api/pdf/report).
findings.evidence: Vercel get_runtime_errors cluster count 42 users 21 routes /api/reports/export, /api/pdf/report; 5xx group_by requestPath /api/pdf/report 6 (single capture before the MCP ban).
findings.why_it_matters: Any PDF a person receives (market report, CMA export) fails at the moment a lead asks for it; docs/PAGE_CONTRACT.md governs these deliverables.
findings.proposed_fix: Add @react-pdf/stylesheet (and the other @react-pdf peer packages) as explicit dependencies or to serverExternalPackages in next.config so the tracer bundles them; add a deploy-health probe that renders one PDF.

questions_for_matt: The database spends more than half of every hour rewriting the 594K-row tile view on what F7 recorded as a 2-core / 1 GB instance. Splitting the view fixes most of it; do you want to fund a Supabase compute upgrade or a read replica on top, or hold at the current tier and accept nightly refresh for closed inventory?

Out-of-market cities (Grants Pass, Klamath Falls, Medford, Ashland, Phoenix) dominate the timed-out search-tile reads and show 10-14 s LCP; should those search pages exist at all, or be noindexed and served from a smaller tile set?
Dead tables hold data from decommissioned systems (fub_person_geo 2,255 rows, content_briefs 987, producer_* tables, open_houses, listings_historical). Drop them, or archive an export first?
